name.en: ANCHOR: Systemic Resilience in a post-BANI Youth Work
name.ka: ANCHOR: სისტემური მდგრადობა ახალგაზრდულ მუშაობაში (BANI-ს შემდგომ სამყაროში)
name.ar: ANCHOR: المرونة المنهجية في العمل الشبابي بعد عالم BANI

deadline_note: SALTO calendar deadline 8 Nov 2026 (24h UTC); selection 22 Nov 2026

summary.en: An Erasmus+ training course in northern Portugal where youth workers build their own resilience and co-create a practical resilience toolkit for young people. Board, lodging and programme are covered and travel is reimbursed.
summary.ka: Erasmus+-ის სასწავლო კურსი ჩრდილოეთ პორტუგალიაში, სადაც ახალგაზრდული მუშაკები საკუთარ მდგრადობას აძლიერებენ და ახალგაზრდებისთვის პრაქტიკულ ხელსაწყოებს ქმნიან. საცხოვრებელი, კვება და პროგრამა დაფარულია, მგზავრობა კი ანაზღაურდება.
summary.ar: دورة تدريبية ضمن Erasmus+ في شمال البرتغال يعزّز فيها العاملون مع الشباب مرونتهم ويصمّمون معاً أدوات عملية للشباب. السكن والطعام والبرنامج مغطاة وتُعوَّض تكاليف السفر.

about.en:
ANCHOR is a five-day Erasmus+ training course (22–28 January 2027, including travel days) in Amarante, northern Portugal, for 24 youth workers from Portugal, France, Spain, Greece, Bulgaria and Malta. It focuses on personal and professional resilience, burnout prevention and recognising mental-health challenges within professional boundaries (including Psychological First Aid).

Methods include nature-based sessions, an experiential mental-health board game, Theatre of the Oppressed, storytelling and World Café. Participants co-create the ANCHOR Resilience Toolkit, an open educational resource tested with students of Escola Secundária de Amarante. The course includes preparation (questionnaire, learning contract with a mentor) and follow-up dissemination at home.

It is organised by Associação Comunidades que Florescem with partners in France, Spain, Greece, Bulgaria and Malta; trainers are Ana Catarina Mendes and Abraham Azzopardi. Participants receive a Youthpass.

en: Hands-on resilience and burnout-prevention training with a co-created toolkit
Nature-based, theatre and game-based non-formal methods
Accommodation and meals covered, travel reimbursed (EUR 285–395), Youthpass

eligibility.en: Youth workers aged 22+ with at least two years of experience who currently work with young people, resident in Portugal, France, Spain, Greece, Bulgaria or Malta (the SALTO listing reserves 4 places for applicants from Spain via Asociación Sociocultural BreGal). Working English required; commitment to preparation, the full week and follow-up. Youth workers supporting young people with fewer opportunities are encouraged.

en: Open the SALTO training page and read the full description.
Create a free SALTO account and log in.
Complete the online application form before 8 November 2026 (24h UTC).
Wait for the selection result (around 22 November 2026) and arrange travel with your sending organisation.

costs.en: Funded by Erasmus+. Accommodation and meals fully covered (arrival dinner to departure breakfast). Travel reimbursed up to EUR 285 (green travel) to EUR 395 depending on the sending country, after documentation and dissemination are completed. The SALTO listing mentions a EUR 30 membership fee for new members of the Spanish partner.

score_reason: Funded, well-designed course; limited to six EU countries and experienced youth workers

name.en: Annual Conference 2027 "Fachkräfte im Blick" — European and International Youth Work Stakeholder Meeting

deadline_note: SALTO calendar deadline 11 Nov 2026; selection 4 Dec 2026

summary.en: The German Erasmus+ Youth National Agency and IJAB invite youth-work professionals to their annual conference in Bonn on training and qualifying staff in European and international youth work. It is held in German with peer cafés, spotlights and thematic workshops.
summary.ka: გერმანიის Erasmus+ ახალგაზრდობის ეროვნული სააგენტო და IJAB ახალგაზრდულ სფეროში მომუშავე პროფესიონალებს ბონში წლიურ კონფერენციაზე იწვევს. ღონისძიება გერმანულ ენაზე ჩატარდება და მოიცავს პირთა გაცვლას, პრეზენტაციებსა და თემატურ სემინარებს.
summary.ar: تدعو الوكالة الوطنية الألمانية لبرنامج Erasmus+ للشباب ومنظمة IJAB المهنيين في العمل الشبابي إلى مؤتمرها السنوي في بون حول تأهيل الكوادر في العمل الشبابي الأوروبي والدولي. يُعقد باللغة الألمانية ويتضمن مقاهي حوار وورش عمل موضوعية.

about.en:
JUGEND für Europa (the German National Agency for Erasmus+ Youth and the European Solidarity Corps) and IJAB (the German specialist centre for international youth work) hold their annual conference "Fachkräfte im Blick" on 17–18 February 2027 at the Gustav-Stresemann-Institut in Bonn. It brings together around 100 professionals and managers from child and youth services in Germany and German-speaking countries, plus researchers and youth-policy representatives.

The programme opens with keynotes from the heads of IJAB and JUGEND für Europa on European and international youth work in the current geopolitical situation, followed by three participatory formats: peer cafés, 'spotlights' where organisations present tools and methods, and thematic workshops with experts. Participants' needs collected at registration shape the programme.

The working language is German. The venue is accessible to people with disabilities.

en: Networking with the main German-speaking actors in European youth work
Participatory format: peer cafés, spotlights, thematic workshops
Accommodation and meals covered by the organisers

eligibility.en: Professionals, trainers, project managers, youth-policy makers and researchers in youth work from Germany, Austria, the German-speaking Community of Belgium, Czechia, Liechtenstein and Luxembourg (as listed on SALTO). Good German is required.

en: Read the event page in the SALTO European Training Calendar.
Log in to SALTO (free account) and submit the registration form, stating your needs and interests.
Apply by 11 November 2026.
Selection is communicated by 4 December 2026; participants from outside Germany coordinate travel reimbursement with their own National Agency.

costs.en: Accommodation and meals covered by the organisers. Participants from Germany receive travel reimbursement minus a EUR 25 participation fee (waived for the Bonn region). For participants from Austria, Belgium, Liechtenstein, Luxembourg and Switzerland, travel reimbursement and any fee are set by their own National Agencies.

score_reason: Niche professional conference in German for a few countries

summary.en: An Erasmus+ study visit at one of Finland's national youth centres for professionals who work with parents under 30. Participants exchange methods for youth work, family work and inclusion, and travel is funded under Erasmus+ rules.
summary.ka: Erasmus+-ის სასწავლო ვიზიტი ფინეთის ერთ-ერთ ეროვნულ ახალგაზრდულ ცენტრში იმ პროფესიონალებისთვის, ვინც 30 წლამდე მშობლებთან მუშაობს. მონაწილეები ახალგაზრდულ და ოჯახურ მუშაობაში მეთოდებს ცვლიან, მგზავრობა კი Erasmus+-ის წესებით ფინანსდება.
summary.ar: زيارة دراسية ضمن Erasmus+ في أحد المراكز الوطنية للشباب في فنلندا للمهنيين العاملين مع آباء وأمهات دون الثلاثين. يتبادل المشاركون أساليب العمل الشبابي والأسري والإدماج، ويُموَّل السفر وفق قواعد Erasmus+.

about.en:
Sharing Paths, Strengthening Families is a study visit hosted by Metsäkartano, one of Finland's national youth centres, specialised in youth work, outdoor and adventure education and international youth work. The SALTO listing gives 6 February 2027 as the date. It gathers about 25 professionals from Erasmus+ programme countries who support young parents (under 30) and young families.

The programme combines study visits, workshops and professional exchange, including a joint exchange day with Finnish professionals. Focus areas are youth work, non-formal learning, inclusion, equal opportunities and cross-sectoral cooperation between youth work, family work and social services.

The organiser states clearly that the activity is for working professionals, not students. Application is through the organiser's form linked on the SALTO page.

en: Hosted by a Finnish national youth centre with strong international experience
Study visits plus a joint exchange day with Finnish practitioners
Travel grant based on the Erasmus+ distance bands

eligibility.en: Youth workers, family-support professionals, social workers and NGO staff from Erasmus+ programme countries who work directly with young parents (especially under 30). Practical experience required; working language English. Not open to students.

en: Read the activity description on the SALTO page.
Fill in the organiser's application form (Google Form linked on the page) by 1 December 2026 (Finnish applicants by 1 January 2027).
Wait for the selection result (by early January 2027).
Book travel within the Erasmus+ travel band for your distance.

costs.en: Erasmus+-funded. Travel grant by distance band (e.g. EUR 211/285 green for 100–499 km, EUR 309/417 for 500–1,999 km, EUR 395/535 for 2,000–2,999 km). Accommodation and meals are expected to be provided by the host; contact the organiser for details.

score_reason: Funded but for experienced professionals only; date details thin

about.en:
The Online Partner Finding Fair is a Training and Cooperation Activity (TCA) run online by DZS, the Czech National Agency for Erasmus+, on 11 November 2026 (15:00–16:30 CET). It is for lower- and upper-secondary teachers (learners aged 13–18) who take part in Erasmus+ KA1 school projects (KA122 short-term or KA120 accredited).

After a short introduction, participants meet potential partners in breakout rooms ('speed dating'), present their projects and exchange contacts, aiming to find hosting schools for pupil or staff mobility, job-shadowing partners or schools for online cooperation.

About 60 places are shared among Czech participants and colleagues from Slovenia, Latvia, Denmark, Cyprus, Croatia, Luxembourg, Austria, Greece, Finland, Türkiye, Poland, Malta, Germany, Portugal and Sweden.

en: Quick way to find partner and hosting schools for KA1 mobility
Online: no travel, 90 minutes
Run by the Czech National Agency (DZS)

eligibility.en: Teachers, educators and school representatives involved in an Erasmus+ KA1 school-education project (learners aged 13–18) from countries whose National Agency is a sending partner: Czechia, Slovenia, Latvia, Denmark, Cyprus, Croatia, Luxembourg, Austria, Greece, Finland, Türkiye, Poland, Malta, Germany, Portugal, Sweden. English.

en: Check that your country's National Agency is listed as a sending partner on the SALTO E&T event page.
Register (free) on the SALTO Education & Training platform and log in.
Submit the TCA participant application on the event page by 3 November 2026.
Your own National Agency selects participants and confirms; it also arranges or reimburses your travel.

score_reason: Short online networking event for teachers already in KA1 projects

summary.ar: لقاء لمدة ثلاثة أيام في أولوموتس لأعضاء شبكة EuroApprentices (متعلمو التعليم المهني الذين أتمّوا تدريبات Erasmus+) من النمسا والتشيك وبولندا وسلوفاكيا، يجمع ورش العمل والتواصل والأنشطة الثقافية.

about.en:
EuroApprentices are vocational students and apprentices who completed an Erasmus+ placement abroad and now promote VET mobility. Their 2026 regional meeting, a Training and Cooperation Activity of the Czech National Agency (DZS), takes place in Olomouc on 4–6 December 2026.

About 40 EuroApprentices (10 per country) plus NA staff from Austria, Czechia, Poland and Slovakia will exchange experiences, build ties through interactive workshops, networking sessions and cultural activities, and plan how to promote the EuroApprentices initiative.

It is one of the few TCAs aimed at learners rather than staff. The deadline is very close: 1 November 2026.

en: One of the few Erasmus+ TCAs aimed at students and apprentices
Workshops, networking and cultural programme
Funded by the National Agencies

eligibility.en: Only existing members of the EuroApprentices network from Austria, Czechia, Poland and Slovakia (about 10 per country). English.

Register (free) on the SALTO Education & Training platform and log in.
Submit the TCA participant application on the event page by 1 November 2026.
Your own National Agency selects participants and confirms; it also arranges or reimburses your travel.

name.ka: ევროპული კონფერენცია „სკოლები გარდამავალ დროში: კეთილდღეობა და სოციალური ერთიანობა ცვალებად ევროპაში“

summary.en: A BarCamp-style Erasmus+ conference in the Ruhr region for 150 school leaders, teachers and support staff on well-being, inclusion and democratic participation in schools. Accommodation and meals are covered by the German National Agency.
summary.ka: BarCamp-ის ფორმატის Erasmus+ კონფერენცია რურის რეგიონში 150 სკოლის ხელმძღვანელისა და მასწავლებლისთვის კეთილდღეობის, ინკლუზიისა და დემოკრატიული მონაწილეობის თემებზე. საცხოვრებელს და კვებას გერმანიის ეროვნული სააგენტო ფარავს.
summary.ar: مؤتمر Erasmus+ بصيغة BarCamp في منطقة الرور لـ150 من مديري المدارس والمعلمين حول الرفاه والإدماج والمشاركة الديمقراطية في المدارس. تتكفّل الوكالة الوطنية الألمانية بالسكن والوجبات.

about.en:
This European conference (19–21 April 2027, Bochum) is a transnational TCA hosted by PAD, the German National Agency for Erasmus+ school education, with the Spanish and Finnish agencies. The Ruhr region's history of industrial change and migration is the backdrop for discussing how schools respond to geopolitical, social and economic transformation.

The format is a BarCamp: participants propose and lead sessions on how Erasmus+ and eTwinning can support inclusion, social cohesion, democratic participation and the well-being and resilience of pupils and teachers. An optional session shows how to start an eTwinning project.

About 150 headteachers, teachers and support staff who are current Erasmus+ beneficiaries will attend. Priority goes to schools with diverse pupils, in disadvantaged or rural areas. Good English is essential.

en: Participant-driven BarCamp with peers from about 18 countries
Focus on well-being, inclusion and democracy in schools
Hotel and meals paid by the German NA, travel by your own NA

eligibility.en: Headteachers, teachers and educational support staff from schools that are current Erasmus+ beneficiaries, in countries whose NA is a sending partner: Germany, Spain, Finland, Poland, Portugal, Iceland, Lithuania, Serbia, Slovakia, Ireland, Austria, Netherlands, Latvia, Sweden, Greece, Denmark, Malta, Belgium (German-speaking Community). Good English required.

Submit the TCA participant application on the event page by 13 December 2026.
Your own National Agency selects participants and confirms; it also arranges or reimburses your travel.

costs.en: Funded through Erasmus+ Training and Cooperation Activities: the organising National Agency covers accommodation, meals and the programme; travel is covered by the participant's sending National Agency.

summary.en: The eighth Cologne conference brings together coordinators of accredited Erasmus+ school mobility consortia to share practice and plan joint mobility, including newcomers from the UK and Switzerland. The German NA pays hotel and meals.
summary.ka: კიოლნის მერვე კონფერენცია Erasmus+-ის აკრედიტებული სასკოლო მობილობის კონსორციუმების კოორდინატორებს აერთიანებს გამოცდილების გასაზიარებლად და ერთობლივი მობილობის დასაგეგმად. სასტუმროსა და კვებას გერმანიის სააგენტო ფარავს.
summary.ar: يجمع مؤتمر كولونيا الثامن منسّقي اتحادات التنقّل المدرسي المعتمدة في Erasmus+ لتبادل الخبرات والتخطيط لتنقّل مشترك، بما في ذلك القادمون الجدد من المملكة المتحدة وسويسرا. تدفع الوكالة الألمانية الفندق والوجبات.

about.en:
This TCA (23–25 May 2027, Cologne) is the eighth conference organised by the German National Agency for school education (PAD) for coordinators of accredited Erasmus+ mobility consortia, preferably those run by school authorities or coordination bodies. With the UK and possibly Switzerland returning to Erasmus+ in 2027, potential coordinators from those countries can also meet European counterparts.

The programme focuses on sharing proven models, partner reliability, inclusion and accessibility, and planning high-quality mobility. Changes in the next programme generation will be discussed, and the European Association of Training Providers (EATP) will attend to discuss course quality.

About 170 places are available, at least three per country.

en: Networking with consortium coordinators from about 20 countries
Preview of the next Erasmus+ programme generation
Hotel (2 nights) and meals paid by the German NA

eligibility.en: Coordinators of accredited Erasmus+ school-education mobility consortia (experienced beneficiaries) from countries whose NA is a sending partner, including Italy, Poland, Malta, Belgium, Latvia, Norway, Denmark, Lithuania, Slovakia, Ireland, Austria, Netherlands, Sweden, Spain, France, Greece, Türkiye and Czechia. English.

Register (free) on the SALTO Education & Training platform and log in.
Submit the TCA participant application on the event page by 4 January 2027.
Your own National Agency selects participants and confirms; it also arranges or reimburses your travel.

costs.en: Funded through Erasmus+ Training and Cooperation Activities: the organising National Agency covers accommodation, meals and the programme; travel is covered by the participant's sending National Agency.

score_reason: Funded but only for consortium coordinators

about.en:
Demystifying Erasmus+ VET Mobility Projects is a Training and Cooperation Activity hosted by Léargas, the Irish National Agency, in Dublin (24–27 January 2027). It is for newcomers and less experienced organisations in vocational education and training (VET) that want to run or apply for Key Action 1 mobility.

Sessions cover KA1 VET rules and compliance, the Erasmus Quality Standards, pre-departure preparation and risk protocols for learners, tracking learning outcomes and impact, and dissemination. Participants draft project ideas with potential partners for upcoming rounds.

Forty places for VET coordinators, international officers, school directors and mobility managers from about 17 countries.

en: Practical KA1 VET project-management toolkit
Partner-building for future mobility rounds
Hosted by the Irish NA in Dublin

about.en:
This contact seminar (18–21 January 2027, Hotel kommod, Ruggell) is organised by AIBA, Liechtenstein's National Agency, for organisations from German-speaking regions in all sectors: school, VET, adult, higher education and youth. The working language is German.

Participants bring their own project idea or join a group, and work through needs analysis, SMART objectives, project structure and RACER indicators, budgeting, impact and dissemination, and how AI can be used acceptably in application writing, ending with all elements needed for a KA220 Cooperation Partnership application. A city tour and visit to the Liechtenstein National Museum in Vaduz are included.

About 78 places, mostly for Liechtenstein, Austria, Germany and German-speaking Belgium, with a few for Italy, Czechia, Slovakia, Slovenia, Luxembourg and Denmark.

Cross-sector networking in German-speaking Europe
3 nights in a single room and all meals covered

Good German required. Recommended for newcomers.

about.en:
This Dutch-language TCA (1–4 February 2027, Amersfoort) is organised by the Netherlands National Agency (Nuffic) around its conference "Samen leren, klaar voor de wereld". It explores how multilingualism, (global) citizenship, internationalisation and resilience come together in daily teaching, and how Erasmus+ and eTwinning can support cooperation on these themes.

It targets schools in regions outside the Randstad (border regions, Wadden Islands, the Caribbean Netherlands), German schools where Dutch is taught, and Flemish schools. Day 2 is a full TCA programme, day 3 the Nuffic conference, day 4 a reflection session.

70 places: about 50 for the Netherlands and 15–17 for Germany; Flemish teachers can express interest by email (tca@erasmusplus.nl).

en: Combines a cross-border TCA with the national Nuffic schools conference
Themes: multilingualism, citizenship, resilience
Conference participation, meals and hotel covered

eligibility.en: Teachers and school leaders of primary, secondary and special schools (pupils 4–18) in the Netherlands (especially outside the Randstad), Germany (schools that teach Dutch) and Flanders. Active, fluent Dutch required.

about.en:
Zorg voor Taal (14–16 April 2027, Hotel The Den, 's-Hertogenbosch) is a TCA of the Netherlands National Agency for teachers and coordinators in vocational (mbo) care and health programmes from the Netherlands and Flanders, working with students aged about 16+.

The seminar covers language competences and (digital) literacy of care students, the use of AI, Dutch and Flemish good practices, and analysis of participants' own institutions' language challenges. The goal is for each participant to meet at least one international partner and agree concrete follow-up, e.g. job shadowing or a small-scale partnership for the first round of the next programme (2028–2034). A study visit to an mbo institution is included.

44 places (22 Netherlands, 22 Flanders).

en: Practical partner-building for Erasmus+ care-sector VET projects
Study visit to a Dutch vocational college
Hotel and meals covered

eligibility.en: Teachers and coordinators in vocational care/health education (students 16+) from the Netherlands and Flanders (Belgium). Experienced Erasmus+ beneficiaries. Fluent Dutch required.

about.en:
First Steps in Erasmus+: Green Skills for School Education is a TCA organised by the Turkish National Agency in Istanbul (7–10 December 2026), part of the long-term activity 'Sustainability and Greening+'. It supports the Erasmus+ priority 'Environment and the fight against climate change'.

Through workshops, collaborative activities and peer learning, primary and secondary school teachers explore how GreenComp, the European sustainability competence framework, translates into teaching and school practice, develop their own sustainability competences and exchange good practice. They also build partnerships for future KA1 and KA2 projects with a green focus.

About 70 participants, from Türkiye and around 13 other Erasmus+ countries.

Partner-building for green KA1/KA2 projects

about.en:
Locked Out is an Erasmus+ youth exchange run by Clube de Jovens Europeus (CJE) in Peniche, Portugal, with around 40 young people from Portugal, Spain, Czechia, Hungary and Slovakia (mobility 25 November – 1 December 2026; travel days 24 November and 2 December). It explores the barriers young people face (no experience, no money, language, gender, background, where you live) and how to get past them.

In international teams, participants pick a real barrier and build an escape room where every puzzle represents part of it, ending with a 'key': a real programme, right, support network or skill. Teams then swap rooms. The programme includes an online preparatory meeting, team-building, an intercultural night, and a follow-up dissemination activity at home. Participants stay at Peniche Surf Camp near Baleal beach and receive a Youthpass.

No experience is needed: puzzles need logic, creativity, building and storytelling, whatever your level of English.

en: Creative, hands-on format: design and build escape rooms
Group travel tickets from national meeting points bought by the organiser
Surf town venue on the Atlantic, Youthpass certificate

eligibility.en: Residents or citizens of Portugal, Spain, Czechia, Hungary or Slovakia, ideally aged 18–25, available for the whole mobility and willing to run a dissemination activity afterwards. Applicants must not currently receive other EU funds (e.g. an Erasmus university grant). No prior experience required.

en: Read the full call on the CJE website.
Apply through the E29 participant portal linked on the page by 1 November 2026 (applications are reviewed daily).
Watch for the selection email (2–10 November 2026) and confirm within 24 hours.
Pay the EUR 50 refundable deposit and join the group's Discord channel for travel details.

costs.en: Travel (from national meeting points), accommodation in shared rooms and three meals a day are co-funded by Erasmus+. Selected participants pay a EUR 50 deposit, refunded after the mobility. Participants bring a European Health Insurance Card; surf lessons are optional at own cost.

score_reason: Fun, fully organised exchange for 18–25s, but only five countries and deadline 1 Nov

about.en:
Digital and Innovative Smart Youth Work brings at least 30 youth workers from eight countries (Italy as host, Morocco, Czechia, Greece, Jordan, Lithuania, Romania and Türkiye) to Mare e Vita Village in Pinarella di Cervia, Italy, on 11–17 December 2026 (including two travel days). It is co-funded by the European Union.

Workshops, simulations, peer learning and group work cover digital tools in youth work, digital storytelling, gamification, virtual facilitation, online safety and AI in youth education. Each participant develops a mini project to apply at home; results feed an open-access digital toolkit and an alumni network.

This call, published by Med-Forum SD (Rabat), is for the four places of the Moroccan group. Applicants from the other partner countries should contact the partner organisation in their own country.

en: Practical digital-youth-work toolkit including AI and online safety
International group from Europe, North Africa and the Middle East
Travel (capped), shared room, three meals, insurance and materials covered

eligibility.en: Youth workers, educators or youth leaders aged 18+ with Moroccan nationality or legal residence in Morocco (4 places), able to work in English, available 11–17 December 2026, with basic digital literacy. No previous experience required; a valid Schengen visa gives priority.

en: Read the project page on the Med-Forum SD website.
Fill in the application form embedded on the page (Google Form) by 17 November 2026.
Make sure your passport and Schengen visa situation allow travel to Italy in December.
Only selected applicants are contacted.

costs.en: Fully funded: international travel refunded up to a fixed budget per person from Morocco; shared room at Mare e Vita Village; three meals a day; accident and liability insurance; all materials.

score_reason: Funded and relevant for MENA youth workers, but only 4 places for Morocco
